Build a missing_taxa_list from an internal data.frame of missing taxa

Source: R/build_missing_taxa_list.R
build_missing_taxa_list.Rd

Build a valid missing_taxa_list from a data.frame describing the taxa to graft (one row per taxon, e.g., read from a .csv file), for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(). Lists of tips (or node IDs, see Details) are written as values of the data.frame, and the function parses them and names every item after the taxa (as required by the grafting functions), and runs all the checks of validity against the backbone phylogeny.

The same data.frame can describe both types of taxa: taxa to graft within a target clade (phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()), and taxa to graft as missing clades sister to a clade (phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()). The function then returns one list per type, built from the same backbone, as done by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy() (see 'Taxa and missing clades in the same data.frame' in Details).

Use phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to read the table directly from an external file.

Clades are defined by tips or node IDs, which allows for fine-tuning the constraints of each taxon (see 'Fine-tuning the clades' in Details). For large phylogenies with neatly defined taxonomic levels, taxonomic tables are likely easier to prepare: see phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy() and phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table().

Usage

build_missing_taxa_list(data, phy, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame, with one row per taxon to graft. Its columns are the items of missing_taxa_list as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(). See Details for a full description. All the columns are read as text. Blank cells and NA are missing values. A column Type ("taxa" or "clades"), or both columns Target_clade and Sister_clade, allow for describing both types of taxa in the same data.frame.

phy

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny on which the taxa will be grafted. It is used to check the tips and clades, and to convert node IDs into tips.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the conversions of node IDs into tips (if any). Default is TRUE.

Value

A missing_taxa_list: a list, ready to be used in the grafting functions, with the following items. If the table describes both types of taxa, a list with two missing_taxa_list: $taxa (with $Target_clade, for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()) and $clades (with $Sister_clade, for phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()).

  • $Taxon_name Character vector.

  • $Target_clade (or $Sister_clade) List of character vectors of tips.

  • $Target_clade_name (or $Sister_clade_name) Only if the column was provided. Character vector of labels (NA if none). Not used for the grafting, but checked against the names of total_richness_per_clades, if provided (see the grafting functions).

  • $include_target_clade_stem Only if the column was provided. Logical vector (NA uses the global argument).

  • $Excluded_subclades Only if the column was provided. List (one element per taxon) of lists of character vectors of tips. NULL for taxa with no excluded subclades. The subclades are named after their labels if Excluded_subclades_names was provided.

  • $exclude_subclades_stem Only if the column was provided. List (one element per taxon) of logical vectors (one value per excluded subclade), or NULL.

  • $allowed_states Only if the column was provided. List (one element per taxon) of character vectors of states, or NULL for taxa without a taxon-level value (the global allowed_states argument is used).

Every item is named after the taxa ($Taxon_name), in the same order.

Details

The columns of data are the items of missing_taxa_list as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(). Column names must be written exactly as below. Tips are separated by commas (,), and the subclades by semicolons (;). Spaces around separators are ignored. Values are TRUE or FALSE (also T, F, yes, no, 1, 0), or NA.

  • Taxon_name (Required): Names of the taxa to graft. Names must be unique and absent from phy$tip.label.

  • Type: (Optional) "taxa" for taxa to graft within a target clade, or "clades" for taxa to graft as missing clades sister to a clade (case is ignored). Only needed to describe both types in the same table with a single clade column (see 'Taxa and missing clades in the same table' below).

  • Target_clade and/or Sister_clade (Required): Tip labels defining a target clade per taxon, i.e., the clade where the taxon is known to belong (e.g., its genus); or a sister clade, i.e., the clade on whose stem branch the taxon is grafted, as its sister. A pair of tips defines the clade as their MRCA node (e.g., "t26, t18"). A single tip defines the "clade" as the terminal branch of this tip (e.g., "t15"). A node ID of phy (digits only, e.g., "34") also defines the clade, see 'Node IDs' below. Use Sister_clade to prepare a list for phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(): the columns specific to phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() below are then ignored, with a warning.

  • include_target_clade_stem: (Optional) Logical values. For each taxon, whether the stem branch of its target clade is available for grafting. NA values and blank cells use the global include_target_clade_stem argument of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa().

  • Excluded_subclades: (Optional) For each taxon, tip labels defining the excluded subclades of its target clade where the taxon is known not to belong. Each subclade is defined by a pair of tips, a single tip, or a node ID. Ex: "t10, t19; 50; t7" for three subclades, the two first being clades with multiple species defined by a pair of tips ("t10, t19"), and an internal node ID ("50"). The last one is a single tip define by its tip label ("t7"). Use blank cells for taxa without excluded subclades.

  • exclude_subclades_stem: (Optional) Logical values. For each taxon, whether the stem of each of its excluded subclades is also excluded, with one value per subclade of Excluded_subclades separated by semicolons, or a single value used for all of them. Ex: "FALSE; TRUE; TRUE". NA values and blank cells use the global exclude_subclades_stem argument of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa().

  • allowed_states: (Optional) For each taxon, the states of a simmap in which it can be grafted (see the simmap argument of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()), separated by commas. It is accepted with both Target_clade and Sister_clade. Ex: "blue, green". Blank cells and NA have no taxon-level value, so the global allowed_states argument of the grafting function is used for the taxon. States are matched exactly with the states of the simmap (e.g., case matters) when grafting, and so cannot contain commas. If the simmap argument is a list of the maps of several traits, give the states of each trait separated by semicolons, in the order of the traits (e.g., "A1, A2;; C3" for three traits: no states for the second trait, so the global allowed_states of the trait, or all its states, are used), or name the traits (e.g., "color=A1,A2; elevation=C3"). The names of the states are not checked here as the simmap is not provided: the grafting function checks them.

Optional columns that do not match items in missing_taxa_list can be used to provide names of clades:

  • Target_clade_name or Sister_clade_name (Optional): Label of the target (or sister) clade. It is only used to check that the clades are defined consistently (see 'Labels of the clades' section below).

  • Excluded_subclades_names (Optional): Labels of the excluded subclades, separated by semicolons, in the same order as in Excluded_subclades. Ex: "group_1; group_2; tip_t7". There must be one label per subclade. If provided, they are used as names of the subclades in the Excluded_subclades item of the list, and in the messages of the grafting functions.

Other columns are ignored, with a warning.

Taxa and missing clades in the same data.frame

A data.frame can describe both types of taxa, so a single call prepares the lists for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(), on the same backbone and with the same clades written with the same tips. The type of each taxon is given by:

  • The column Type, with "taxa" (target clade) or "clades" (sister clade): the clade is then read from Target_clade or Sister_clade, respectively.

  • Otherwise, without Type, by the clade column that is filled in its row, when the data.frame has both Target_clade and Sister_clade columns. Each row must fill exactly one of them (the function stops if both or none are filled).

The columns specific to a type are only read for the taxa of this type (e.g., Excluded_subclades for taxa with a target clade), and are ignored for the others, with a warning if they are filled. allowed_states is read for both types. A clade written in the column of the other type than Type is ignored with a warning.

The function returns:

  • A single missing_taxa_list if all the taxa have the same type, whether Type is provided or not.

  • A list of two missing_taxa_list, named $taxa and $clades, if both types are present. Each one is a standard missing_taxa_list, and the taxa of both lists are named differently (names must be unique across the table). Use $taxa in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and $clades in phylograftR::graft_missing_clades().

Clade labels are also checked across both lists (the same clade has the same label as a target clade and as a sister clade), so that they can be matched with the names of total_richness_per_clades.

Recommended use: provide the whole list ($taxa and $clades) to phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(), which grafts the missing taxa first and then the missing clades, with a single set of inputs. The two steps can also be chained by hand: graft the missing taxa with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(), then use the grafted phylogeny as the backbone to graft the missing clades with phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(). The clades are defined by tips of the backbone, so they stay valid even when the grafted phylogeny is used for the second step.

Node IDs

Clades (Target_clade, Sister_clade, and each subclade of Excluded_subclades) are typically defined by (pairs of) tips. However, the function also accepts clades defined by the ID of a node of phy instead of tips, in the same table, and even in the same cell (e.g., "50; t5, t12; t7" for three excluded subclades defined respectively by an internal node, a pair of tips, a terminal tip label). Node IDs are integers: 1 to N, with N being the number of tips (ape::Ntip(phy)) correspond to terminal nodes, and thus define single-tip clades. Following IDs are the internal nodes, as shown by ape::nodelabels(), and correspond to clades with multiple descending species.

A value made only of digits is a node ID, so tip labels must include at least one other character than digits to be distinguished. A clade is defined by tips or by one node ID, not both, and one node ID defines the clade alone. Node IDs are converted into tips before any other check, as done by phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips(), and the conversions are printed if verbose = TRUE.

The warnings and errors that follow, and the grafting functions, therefore use the tips that are traced back to your node IDs in the messages. If a clade is already defined by tips in the table, a node ID of the same clade is converted into the same tips. Convert total_richness_per_clades (if you use it) at the same time as the list, with phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips(), so the tips of the clades match between both objects. Alternatively, build it from a table of clades with phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades(), which matches the clades with those of the missing_taxa_list.

Fine-tuning the clades

Defining clades with tips or node IDs gives full control on the constraints of each taxon. Any node of phy can be used as a Target_clade, as a Sister_clade, or as an excluded subclade, simply by writing its node ID (e.g., "34"), or two tips whose MRCA is the node (e.g., "t8, t7"). The node does not need to match a taxonomic group: it can be a clade without a name, a clade that groups several taxonomic units (e.g., two neighboring genera), a part of a taxonomic group only, or a clade you identified from the phylogeny itself or from another source (e.g., a molecular study). Clades can be nested at any depth, and each taxon has its own set of excluded subclades, with or without their stem.

This is the best route to fine-tune the grafting of a limited number of taxa, but the clades have to be written for each taxon. When the backbone is large, and taxonomic levels (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus) are defined for its tips and for the taxa to graft, taxonomic tables are the go-to option: clades are retrieved from their taxonomic names, which ease the attribution of clades across many taxa. See phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table() and phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy().

Both routes return the same missing_taxa_list, so they can be combined: build a list from taxonomic tables, and then adjust the clades of a few taxa with node IDs or tips.

Labels of the clades

Labels (Target_clade_name, Sister_clade_name, and Excluded_subclades_names) are optional but, when used, they identify the clades across all the rows of the table: the same clade must always have the same label, and different clades must have different labels. A clade is identified by the MRCA node of its tips in phy, so the same clade can be defined by different pairs of tips, as long as they share this MRCA node. The function stops if a label is used for different clades, or if a clade is given different labels, and lists the labels and tips in conflict. This catches typos in the tips or in the labels. Subclades without a label are not checked.

Validity checks

The function stops with an informative message if:

  • Required columns are missing, or one Taxon_name is missing, duplicated, or already in phy.

  • A clade has no tips, or tips are repeated, or are absent from phy.

  • The number of values in exclude_subclades_stem, or of labels in Excluded_subclades_names, does not match the number of excluded subclades.

  • Labels are inconsistent (see above).

  • A cell of allowed_states has an empty state (check the commas) or repeated states.

  • An excluded subclade is identical to, or contains, the target clade of its taxon (no branch would remain). A warning is issued if it is outside of the target clade (the exclusion has no effect).

The messages give the names of the problematic taxa and the numbers of the rows in the table.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to read the table directly from an external file.

  • phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table() to read the taxonomic tables from external files.

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy() to build a missing_taxa_list from taxonomic tables, with clades defined by taxonomic names instead of tips or node IDs.

  • phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips() to convert the node IDs of a list built 'by hand' into pairs of tips defining their MRCA.

  • phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() and phylograftR::import_total_richness_per_clades() to prepare total_richness_per_clades for the unsampled species.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades using the list.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades using the list.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

Author

Examples

# Load a table of missing taxa as a data.frame in R
file_path <- system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa.csv", package = "phylograftR")
missing_taxa_table <- read.csv(file_path)

# Convert it into a 'missing_taxa_list', checking it against the backbone phylogeny
missing_taxa_list <- build_missing_taxa_list(data = missing_taxa_table, phy = toy_backbone)
# Items are named after the taxa, tips are split, and excluded subclades are named
str(missing_taxa_list, 2)
#> List of 6
#>  $ Taxon_name               : chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Target_clade             :List of 7
#>   ..$ New_sp1: chr [1:2] "t26" "t18"
#>   ..$ New_sp2: chr [1:2] "t26" "t18"
#>   ..$ New_sp3: chr [1:2] "t26" "t18"
#>   ..$ New_sp4: chr [1:2] "t8" "t22"
#>   ..$ New_sp5: chr [1:2] "t8" "t7"
#>   ..$ New_sp6: chr "t5"
#>   ..$ New_sp7: chr [1:2] "t5" "t12"
#>  $ Target_clade_name        : Named chr [1:7] "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_B" ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ include_target_clade_stem: Named logi [1:7] TRUE TRUE FALSE NA TRUE NA ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Excluded_subclades       :List of 7
#>   ..$ New_sp1:List of 2
#>   ..$ New_sp2:List of 2
#>   ..$ New_sp3: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp4: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp5:List of 1
#>   ..$ New_sp6: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp7: NULL
#>  $ exclude_subclades_stem   :List of 7
#>   ..$ New_sp1: Named logi [1:2] TRUE FALSE
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "Subfam_A1" "Tribe_A2a"
#>   ..$ New_sp2: Named logi [1:2] FALSE TRUE
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "Tribe_A2a" "Gen_3"
#>   ..$ New_sp3: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp4: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp5: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp6: NULL
#>   ..$ New_sp7: NULL

# A table can also be built in R and then converted to a valid 'missing_taxa_list' object
my_table <- data.frame(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"),
                       Target_clade = c("t26, t18", "t5"),
                       Excluded_subclades = c("t10, t19; t26, t4", NA),
                       Excluded_subclades_names = c("group_1; group_2", NA))
my_missing_taxa_list <- build_missing_taxa_list(data = my_table, phy = toy_backbone)
str(my_missing_taxa_list, 2)
#> List of 3
#>  $ Taxon_name        : chr [1:2] "M1" "M2"
#>  $ Target_clade      :List of 2
#>   ..$ M1: chr [1:2] "t26" "t18"
#>   ..$ M2: chr "t5"
#>  $ Excluded_subclades:List of 2
#>   ..$ M1:List of 2
#>   ..$ M2: NULL

# Clades can also be defined by node IDs (digits only), alone or mixed with tips.
# Node IDs are converted into tips, and the conversions are printed.
ape::plot.phylo(toy_backbone, cex = 0.7, no.margin = TRUE)
ape::nodelabels(cex = 0.6, frame = "none", col = "blue")

my_table_nodes <- data.frame(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"),
                             Target_clade = c("34", "t5, t12"),
                             Excluded_subclades = c("50", NA))
str(build_missing_taxa_list(data = my_table_nodes, phy = toy_backbone), 2)
#> 2 node ID(s) converted into tips (a tip node gives its tip, an internal node gives one pair of tips with this MRCA node):
#>   - node 34 (internal node, 9 tips) -> t8, t7   [Target_clade: M1]
#>   - node 50 (internal node, 3 tips) -> t13, t27   [Excluded_subclades: M1]
#> List of 3
#>  $ Taxon_name        : chr [1:2] "M1" "M2"
#>  $ Target_clade      :List of 2
#>   ..$ M1: chr [1:2] "t8" "t7"
#>   ..$ M2: chr [1:2] "t5" "t12"
#>  $ Excluded_subclades:List of 2
#>   ..$ M1:List of 1
#>   ..$ M2: NULL

# A table can describe both types of taxa: here, with a column 'Type'.
# Taxa to graft within a target clade and taxa to graft as missing clades
# are returned as two lists, for the two grafting functions.
my_table_both <- data.frame(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3"),
                            Type = c("taxa", "taxa", "clades"),
                            Target_clade = c("t26, t18", "t5, t12", NA),
                            Sister_clade = c(NA, NA, "t10, t19"),
                            Excluded_subclades = c("t26, t4", NA, NA))
lists <- build_missing_taxa_list(data = my_table_both, phy = toy_backbone)
str(lists, 2)
#> List of 2
#>  $ taxa  :List of 3
#>   ..$ Taxon_name        : chr [1:2] "M1" "M2"
#>   ..$ Target_clade      :List of 2
#>   ..$ Excluded_subclades:List of 2
#>  $ clades:List of 2
#>   ..$ Taxon_name  : chr "M3"
#>   ..$ Sister_clade:List of 1

# Without 'Type', each row fills the clade column of its type
my_table_both$Type <- NULL
identical(build_missing_taxa_list(data = my_table_both, phy = toy_backbone), lists)
#> [1] TRUE
